what: The version seam of the TSavo bridge replay (certs/eth-tsavo-bridge.json, gaps), measured. TSavo's Bridge.ethIsFalse_of_claim takes as hypothesis OpenAI's challenge statement as TSavo's file states it (def Claim := ∀ k, 2 ≤ k → ClaimAt k), elaborated on Lean v4.33.1 with Anthropic's Mathlib 0df444a3; OpenAI proved exact_count_and_sat on Lean v4.34.1 with Mathlib d13f23b7 (certs/eth-kernel.json). The bytes are the same (the statement check); this record asks whether the ELABORATED statements are the same term, and so is every definition they can unfold to. It does not re-check any proof.
campaign: eth-refutation; the TSavo bridge lane, its version-seam gap; decided by tools/record-eth-seam.js from a GitHub-hosted run of .github/workflows/eth-seam.yml

words.IDENTICAL: Claim on Anthropic's side, ClaimAt unfolded once, is the same kernel term as exact_count_and_sat's statement on OpenAI's side, and every constant of the two closures is present on both sides as the same kernel term
words.DIFFERENT: anything else; every difference listed and classified (proof-internal, proof-reach, definitional), the verdict never softened by the classes

kernelTerm: the Expr structure: de Bruijn indices, constant names, universe levels with each parameter by its position, literals, projections; binder names, binder infos and metadata dropped (the kernel drops them). Surface: with them. Proof-erased: every subterm whose type is a proposition (Meta.isProof) replaced by one marker, and the closure taken over what remains
closure: from the root: definitions and opaques with their type and value; theorems with their statement only (proofs never followed); axioms and Quot with their type; inductives with their type, constructors, recursor, mutual block and, for a structure, its projection functions; constructors with their inductive; recursors with every rule's right-hand side. The proof-erased closure follows only what survives erasure, so it reaches no theorem

openai.project: corpus/eth-refutation/bridge/openai (autoImplicit false, as OpenAI's lakefile) + the two statement modules

anthropic.project: anthropics/formal-math@16a5ce41 eth/ with TSavo's bridge/ as eth-tsavo.yml sets it up (README block + the declared challenge-lib amendment) + the challenge module

why: the two statements are the same kernel term (only a binder name differs: hk against an anonymous arrow binder), all 74 OAI constants of the challenge are the same kernel terms on both sides, but the closures are not: of 2585 common constants 308 differ, and 104 are present on one side only (305 definitional, 106 proof-reach, 1 proof-internal). Lean's kernel, reading each side's terms in the other environment, identifies 61 of the differing constants both ways and 199 one way. By cause (our reading, every one of the 412 differences): identified by the kernel both ways 61, in one closure only, identical in the other environment 1, the Monoid hierarchy's new shape in Mathlib 231, the moved files that construct ℝ, ℂ and NNReal 94, Lean core's Bool.and 2, a rename under the real power 10, NNReal's Nonneg 12, a proof-only binder order 1. 8 of the 151 constants the statement names directly differ: Monoid.toNPow, Real.instAdd, Real.instDivInvMonoid, Real.instLE, Real.instLT, Real.instMul, Real.instOne, Real.instZero. Modulo proofs: DIFFERENT

headline.compares: Claim (TSavo's file, Anthropic's side, ClaimAt unfolded once) against exact_count_and_sat's statement (OpenAI's file, OpenAI's side); closures without Claim, ClaimAt and exact_count_and_sat

vocabulary.note: the constants the statement is written in: the challenge's own OAI definitions, and every constant their types and values name directly (instances included)

kernelAcrossSides.note: each side's term read in the other environment (SeamCross): identified = same, same up to binder names, or definitionally equal there by Lean's kernel (theorem _ : foreign = local := Eq.refl accepted)

moved-file.reading: The files that construct ℝ, ℂ and NNReal moved (Mathlib/Data/Real/Basic.lean → Mathlib/Basic/Real/Basic.lean, likewise Complex.Basic and NNReal.Defs). Private definitions (Real.add, Real.mul, Real.le, Real.inv', …) and the irreducible_def wrappers (Real.definition._@…, Real.wrapped._@…) carry their module in their names, so the same definitions appear under different names on the two sides, and the instances that use them (Real.instAdd, Real.instLE, …) name constants the other environment does not have.

monoid-hierarchy.reading: Mathlib's Monoid hierarchy changed shape between the two commits. In 0df444a3 (Anthropic's side) Monoid.mk takes a Semigroup and MulOneClass.mk a MulOne (AddMonoid, AddZeroClass likewise); in d13f23b7 (OpenAI's side) Monoid.mk takes One, Mul and mul_assoc directly and MulOneClass.mk takes One and Mul (Monoid.toMul, AddMonoid.toAdd, MulOneClass.toOne, … exist only there). The fields are the same propositions, but the structures carrying them are different inductive types, so every instance built with these constructors (on ℕ, ℚ, ℝ, ℂ, NNReal, Multiset: Real.commRing among them) and every statement projecting through them is a different term. Where Anthropic's term only projects (an instance path through Monoid.toSemigroup), it reads in d13f23b7 and the kernel identifies it there; where it builds a Monoid, it does not type-check there.

kernel-identified.reading: The two terms differ, mostly in instance paths (which chain of parent projections reaches an instance: DivisionSemiring.toSemiring against CommSemiring.toSemiring from the same Field, in the Cauchy-sequence construction of ℝ), and Lean's kernel, reading each side's term in the other environment, finds them definitionally equal there, both ways.

lean-core.reading: Lean core: Bool.and is compiled through the matcher Bool.and.match_1 in v4.33.1 and directly by Bool.rec in v4.34.1; OpenAI's Bool.and, read in Anthropic's environment, is definitionally equal there.

renamed.reading: A rename used by Real.sinOrderIso (so by Real.arcsin, Complex.arg, Complex.log, the real power): Equiv.setCongr and OrderIso.setCongr (0df444a3, universe parameters changed) against Set.equivOfEq and Set.orderIsoOfEq (d13f23b7).

nonneg.reading: NNReal's carrier: d13f23b7 has a definition Nonneg for the subtype {x // 0 ≤ x} that the NNReal instances name; 0df444a3 writes the subtype directly.

binder-order.reading: An auxiliary proof whose implicit binders {a} and [SemilatticeSup α] come in the other order; only proofs reach it.

elsewhere-identified.reading: Present in one closure only, but the constant exists in the other environment and the kernel identifies it there; the other side's terms simply reach the same instance by another path.

chain.note: the headline factored: the same text on the two sides, then the declared change (theorem → def ClaimAt + def Claim) on each side

classes.proof-internal: the constant differs, but after proof erasure the two terms are the same (the kernel identifies proofs of one proposition)
classes.proof-reach: in neither proof-erased closure: only proofs reach it (a theorem's statement, or a definition only a proof mentions), so it cannot change what the statement says
classes.definitional: differs outside proofs, or is present on one side only inside the proof-erased closure: the statement's meaning may depend on it

gaps: The comparison is of terms, not of meanings: two different kernel terms can still denote the same proposition; DIFFERENT says only that the terms differ, and the classes say where.

The kernel check across the sides is constant by constant: a foreign term is read with the LOCAL meaning of every constant it names. It identifies differences of instance paths and of compilation; it cannot identify two different inductive types (the Monoid constructors of the two Mathlibs), so ℝ's ring and field structures stay unidentified, and no single kernel has checked that the two statements are the same proposition.
The groups are our reading of the diffs, by name patterns written after reading them (GROUPS in this tool); the kernel statuses and the diffs beside each difference are the evidence.

Proof erasure trusts Meta.isProof on each subterm (Lean's elaborator-side type inference, not the kernel); an erase error is counted in each export header (eraseErrors) and keeps the subterm, which can only add differences, never hide one.

The exports are written by our metaprogram running inside each Lean; a bug in it that is the same on both sides would hide nothing it serialises faithfully but could miss a field it does not serialise: the kernel-relevant fields written are kind, universe parameters, type, value, safety, mutual block, inductive/constructor/recursor counts and flags, and recursor rules.

OpenAI's side is our project on OpenAI's toolchain and Mathlib (as corpus/eth-refutation/bridge/openai), not openai/math itself: the challenge module imports Mathlib alone, so the other dependencies of openai/math cannot reach its elaboration; the package option is autoImplicit false, as theirs.
